title: Training Q&A — Guest Stays Running Past the Handling Date in a Utility Pass-Through Service Final-Statement Projection
content:
**Rule.** For a prepayment of the estimated final Utility Pass-Through Service statement, where the most recently begun guest stay registered with the community has a planned last day after the handling date, the projected daily use is multiplied by 125 percent (a multiplier of 1.25) when that planned last day falls fourteen or more days after the stay's first day and by 110 percent (a multiplier of 1.1) when it falls fewer than fourteen days after it; without a registered guest stay running past the handling date no guest share applies to the projection.

Guest stays are registered on the site's Community Rules & Site Care records, each with a first day and a planned last day.

## Questions answered

**Q. Which stay is looked at?** The most recently begun registered stay — the one with the latest first day.

**Q. When does it "run past the handling date"?** When its planned last day is after the handling date. A planned last day on the handling date itself is not after it.

**Q. How is the length measured?** The planned last day less the first day, in days: 14 or more gives 125 percent, fewer than 14 gives 110 percent.

**Q. Where does the share act?** It multiplies the projected daily use, before the projected final-cycle consumption is priced.

**Q. Worked through (handling date 10 June, hypothetical).**

| Most recently begun registered stay | Planned last day after 10 June? | Length | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 June to 20 June | Yes | 19 days | 125 percent |
| 5 June to 18 June | Yes | 13 days | 110 percent |
| 5 June to 19 June | Yes | 14 days | 125 percent |
| 25 May to 10 June | No (ends on the handling date) | 16 days | none |
| 2 May to 9 May | No | 7 days | none |

With a projected daily use of 0.14 kgal and the 1 June to 20 June stay: 0.14 times 1.25 is 0.175 kgal a day.
